addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

input.prompt:
I need to trace how a browser request for another user's profile image (avatar) is served in this codebase — from the HTTP route/handler all the way down to the data/storage layer.

Search very thoroughly for:
1. Routes or handlers that serve user profile images or avatars (look for URL patterns like /avatar, /profile/image, /user/*/avatar, etc.)
2. The handler function that processes these requests
3. Any service or controller layer it calls
4. Any data access / storage layer it reaches

Look in route definitions, controllers, handlers, services, repositories, and storage-related code. Check for terms like "avatar", "profile image", "profile picture", "photo", "user image". Also check for file serving or blob serving handlers.

Report every file path and function/symbol name involved in the chain from HTTP request to stored data. Be very thorough — check multiple naming conventions.

content.text: I now have all the pieces to provide a comprehensive trace. Here is the complete report. --- ## Complete Request Trace: User Avatar Serving ### Overview This is the "usememos/memos" project (Go backend + React frontend). User avatars are stored as **base64-encoded data URIs** directly in the `avatar_url` column of the `user` database table. They are NOT stored as files on disk or in object storage. The serving path is a straightforward HTTP handler that reads the user record from the database, decodes the data URI, and returns the raw image bytes. --- ### Layer 1: Route Registration **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 121-125) The `RegisterRoutes` method registers two file-serving routes on the Echo HTTP server: ```go func (s *FileServerService) RegisterRoutes(echoServer *echo.Echo) { fileGroup := echoServer.Group("/file") fileGroup.GET("/attachments/:uid/:filename", s.serveAttachmentFile) fileGroup.GET("/users/:identifier/avatar", s.serveUserAvatar) } ``` **URL pattern:** `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar` The `:identifier` path parameter is the **username** of the target user. **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/server.go` (lines 80-82) This route is registered during server startup in `NewServer()`: ```go fileServerService := fileserver.NewFileServerService(s.Profile, s.Store, s.Secret) fileServerService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer) ``` --- ### Layer 2: HTTP Handler **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 168-210) **Function:** `FileServerService.serveUserAvatar` The handler performs these steps in sequence: 1. **Authentication check (private instance only):** If the instance has no `InstanceURL` set (private mode), it calls `s.getCurrentUser()` which delegates to `Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser()`. Anonymous requests are rejected with 401. On public instances (InstanceURL is set), anonymous access is permitted. 2. **Extract username:** Reads the `:identifier` path parameter from the URL. 3. **Look up user:** Calls `s.getUserByUsername(ctx, identifier)` which calls `s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{Username: &identifier})`. 4. **Validate avatar exists:** Checks `user.AvatarURL != ""`. Returns 404 if empty. 5. **Parse data URI:** Calls `s.parseDataURI(user.AvatarURL)` which uses a regex to extract the MIME type and base64-decode the image data from the `data:image/png;base64,...` string. 6. **Validate MIME type:** Checks the image type against `avatarAllowedTypes` (png, jpeg, jpg, gif, webp, heic, heif). 7. **Respond:** Sets security headers, Content-Type, Cache-Control (`public, max-age=3600`), and returns the raw image bytes via `c.Blob()`. --- ### Layer 3: Authentication **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 708-712) **Function:** `FileServerService.getCurrentUser` ```go func (s *FileServerService) getCurrentUser(ctx context.Context, c *echo.Context) (*store.User, error) { authHeader := c.Request().Header.Get(echo.HeaderAuthorization) cookieHeader := c.Request().Header.Get("Cookie") return s.authenticator.AuthenticateToUser(ctx, authHeader, cookieHeader) } ``` **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/auth/authenticator.go` (lines 190-208) **Function:** `Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser` Authentication priority: 1. **Bearer token** from `Authorization` header (Access Token V2 or Personal Access Token) 2. **Refresh token cookie** fallback (for browser `` tag requests that can't set Authorization headers) **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/auth/extract.go` (lines 11-33) **Functions:** `ExtractBearerToken`, `ExtractRefreshTokenFromCookie` -- parse raw header values. --- ### Layer 4: User Lookup (by username) **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 715-717) **Function:** `FileServerService.getUserByUsername` ```go func (s *FileServerService) getUserByUsername(ctx context.Context, identifier string) (*store.User, error) { return s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{Username: &identifier}) } ``` --- ### Layer 5: Store (Business Logic / Caching) **File:** `/bench/home/work/store/user.go` (lines 148-169) **Function:** `Store.GetUser` - First checks the in-memory cache (`s.userCache`) if searching by ID (not applicable for username lookups). - Falls through to `Store.ListUsers` which calls the database driver. - Caches the result by user ID for subsequent lookups. **File:** `/bench/home/work/store/user.go` (lines 136-146) **Function:** `Store.ListUsers` -- calls `s.driver.ListUsers(ctx, find)` and populates the cache. --- ### Layer 6: Cache **File:** `/bench/home/work/store/store.go` (line 28) The `userCache` is a `*cache.Cache` with default TTL of 10 minutes and max 1000 items. Note: for the avatar flow, cache lookup by ID is bypassed since the query is by username, so it always hits the database driver. --- ### Layer 7: Database Driver (Data Access) Three driver implementations, all reading from the `avatar_url` column of the `user` table: **SQLite:** `/bench/home/work/store/db/sqlite/user.go` (lines 88-205) - **Function:** `DB.ListUsers` - SQL: `SELECT id, username, role, email, nickname, password_hash, avatar_url, description, created_ts, updated_ts, row_status FROM user WHERE username = ? ...` - Scans `avatar_url` into `user.AvatarURL` **PostgreSQL:** `/bench/home/work/store/db/postgres/user.go` (lines 87-195) - **Function:** `DB.ListUsers` - SQL: `SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM "user" WHERE username = $1 ...` **MySQL:** `/bench/home/work/store/db/mysql/user.go` (lines 84-186) - **Function:** `DB.ListUsers` - SQL: `SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ? ...` --- ### Layer 8: Data URI Parsing **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 737-750) **Function:** `FileServerService.parseDataURI` Uses the regex `^data:(?P[^;]+);base64,(?P.+)` to extract the MIME type and base64-encoded payload, then decodes the base64 string into raw bytes. --- ### Layer 9: Private Instance Gate **File:** `/bench/home/work/internal/profile/profile.go` (lines 40-48) **Function:** `Profile.AllowAnonymous` Returns `true` only when `InstanceURL` is set (non-empty after trimming). On a private instance with no InstanceURL, anonymous avatar requests are blocked. --- ### How the Avatar URL Reaches the Frontend **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go` (lines 16-42) **Function:** `convertUserFromStore` When converting a `store.User` to the API protobuf `User` message, if the user's `AvatarURL` is a valid base64 data URI, it is **replaced** with a file-serving path: ```go if user.AvatarURL != "" { _, _, err := extractImageInfo(user.AvatarURL) if err == nil { userpb.AvatarUrl = fmt.Sprintf("/file/%s/avatar", userpb.Name) } else { userpb.AvatarUrl = user.AvatarURL } } ``` Where `userpb.Name` is `"users/"`, so the final URL becomes `/file/users//avatar`. If the stored AvatarURL is NOT a data URI (e.g., an external HTTP URL), it is passed through as-is. **File:** `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx` The frontend `UserAvatar` component renders an `` tag with `src={avatarUrl || "/full-logo.webp"}`, which triggers the browser GET request to `/file/users//avatar`. --- ### Avatar Upload Path (how data gets stored) **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service.go` (lines 335-354) In `UpdateUser`, when the update mask includes `"avatar_url"`, the handler: 1. Validates the data URI format via `extractImageInfo()` 2. Validates the MIME type against an allowlist (png, jpeg, jpg, gif, webp) 3. Sets `update.AvatarURL = &request.User.AvatarUrl` 4. Calls `s.Store.UpdateUser(ctx, update)` which writes the full data URI string to the `avatar_url` column --- ### Complete Call Chain Summary ``` Browser: GET /file/users/{username}/avatar | v [Echo Router] -> fileserver.FileServerService.RegisterRoutes() | /bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121 v fileserver.FileServerService.serveUserAvatar() | /bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168 | +-- [Auth check on private instances] | FileServerService.getCurrentUser() :708 | -> auth.Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser() | /bench/home/work/server/auth/authenticator.go:190 | -> auth.ExtractBearerToken() /server/auth/extract.go:11 | -> auth.ExtractRefreshTokenFromCookie() /server/auth/extract.go:23 | +-- FileServerService.getUserByUsername() :715 | -> store.Store.GetUser() | /bench/home/work/store/user.go:148 | -> store.Store.ListUsers() :136 | -> Driver.ListUsers() (interface: /bench/home/work/store/driver.go:47) | sqlite: /bench/home/work/store/db/sqlite/user.go:88 | postgres: /bench/home/work/store/db/postgres/user.go:87 | mysql: /bench/home/work/store/db/mysql/user.go:84 | SQL: SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ? | +-- FileServerService.parseDataURI(user.AvatarURL) :737 | Regex decode: data:{mime};base64,{payload} -> (mimeType, []byte) | +-- Validate mime against avatarAllowedTypes :75-83 | +-- Set security headers, Cache-Control, Content-Type | setSecurityHeaders() :758 | +-- c.Blob(http.StatusOK, imageType, imageData) :209 ``` --- ### Key Data Model **File:** `/bench/home/work/store/user.go` (lines 29-45) The `store.User` struct has field `AvatarURL string` (line 43). This holds the **full data URI** (e.g., `data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo...`). The avatar image bytes live entirely inside the database row -- there is no separate file or blob storage for avatars. **File:** `/bench/home/work/proto/api/v1/user_service.proto` (lines 228-229) The protobuf `User` message has `string avatar_url = 6`, which in API responses contains the `/file/users/{username}/avatar` path (not the raw data URI).
